parameters.content:
## Send handwritten cards from approved Google Sheets rows

Scribble turns a reviewed Google Sheets mailing row into a handwritten card for a US recipient. Use it for customer thank-you notes or another campaign your team has approved. Fill the complete row first, then change its approval column to approved. The trigger watches that column.

This template uses built-in n8n nodes, including HTTP Request, and needs no community package. It imports inactive with the final send request disabled. Connect Google Sheets, select the document and tab, and follow the setup note below. Keep postal ZIP codes as text so leading zeroes survive.

An enabled send calls Scribble's real API. A scheduled card costs one Scribble credit; a held card is not charged and needs review. The filter accepts complete US mailings with finished messages of 1–500 characters, no recorded card code, and a fixed approval timestamp less than 23 hours old.

The same reference is used as the idempotency key. Scribble retains that key for 24 hours. Never refresh approved_at or retry the sender alone to bypass the filter.

Add a source writeback step before unattended sending. Save the returned id and status, including held results. This template has no durable outbox or result-writing node. Connections and live source payloads still need testing in your account.

## Configure the source and Scribble connection

Create Google Sheets columns with the exact keys below. Keep ZIP and approved_at as plain text. Select your document and tab in Approved mailing rows. campaign_id plus send_id must identify one intended card across all spreadsheets in this Scribble account. Enter every field before changing approval to approved. Editing a message after approval is not a new approval event.

Create an n8n Header Auth credential: Name = Authorization; Value = Bearer followed by a space and your Scribble API key. Select it in the disabled HTTP Request node. The key needs cards:send. Add cards:read if you will use the API for catalogue or card-status reads. Store the key only in Credentials. Use your source provider's own credential selector separately. Scribble account and API documentation: https://scribblecards.com/docs/api

The following is a deliberately blocked setup example, not a real recipient. Replace placeholders with reviewed source values. Use actual design and handwriting IDs from your Scribble account. Optional line2, email and card_code may be empty. Email is used only for the do-not-mail check and is not printed.

```json
{
  "campaign_id": "thankyou-v1",
  "send_id": "REPLACE_EVENT_ID",
  "approval": "approved",
  "approved_at": "REPLACE_FIXED_UTC_APPROVAL_TIME",
  "country": "US",
  "name": "REPLACE_RECIPIENT_NAME",
  "line1": "REPLACE_STREET",
  "line2": "",
  "city": "REPLACE_CITY",
  "state": "REPLACE_STATE",
  "zip": "REPLACE_ZIP",
  "email": "",
  "message": "REPLACE_REVIEWED_MESSAGE",
  "design_id": "REPLACE_DESIGN_ID",
  "handwriting": "REPLACE_HANDWRITING_ID",
  "card_code": ""
}
```

approved_at must be the original approval time in UTC, for example the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ. Persist it once; never use the current execution time on retry. Keep approved values immutable. State must be a valid two-letter US state, territory or military code; ZIP must be five digits, optionally followed by a ZIP+4. The API performs final address, message, design and suppression checks.

Identity components allow letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, up to 48 characters each. The reference is n8n:sheets:mailing:<campaign_id>:<send_id>. It stays unchanged when card contents change, so an inconsistent replay can be rejected while the key is retained.

Keep sending disabled while checking the source, mapping and filter. Before enabling unattended mail, add a writeback step that stores the HTTP response id in card_code and records status in the source. A held card retains its code and needs review. Serialize work for the same identity. The Set node freezes only this execution; it does not lock your spreadsheet. After an uncertain response or an expired approval, reconcile the stable reference and Scribble order history before deciding whether another card is needed.
